I am 74, and at my age I farm in a steady way, not a risky way. I have only 6 mu, some labor in my family is away working, and I do have well irrigation, so I will keep the plan simple and manageable. Cotton is still my main crop, so I will put the largest share of land into cotton because it matches my usual system and I know how to handle it well. I will still keep some wheat and maize because they spread risk, support household grain needs, and fit local practice. I will use better seed where it matters, but I will not push fertilizer and spraying too hard because I want stable yield, lower trouble, and work I can still handle. With irrigation available, I will water at the key stages instead of depending only on rain. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it saves effort compared with deeper ploughing and is easier for me to manage now.
